t:
The analysis of sections for chapter 19 of title 2, Canal Zone Code, preceding section 451 of that chapter, is amended by striking out


“471. Declaration and findings.”


and


“472. Construction, maintenance, and operation of bridge.”

fable.w: This section is a purely clerical amendment that strikes two entries from the analysis of sections for a chapter of the Canal Zone Code. The tempting reading is that "Declaration and findings" or the bridge heading might imply some public process, but these are only headings being deleted. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical legislative amendment that instructs the removal of specific section titles from a code analysis or table of contents. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input. The mention of 'Construction, maintenance, and operation of bridge' is merely the title of the section being removed, not a directive for public participation in such activities.
qwen_block.s: The analysis of sections for chapter 19 of title 2, Canal Zone Code, preceding section 451 of that chapter, is amended by striking out “471. Declaration and findings.” and “472. Construction, maintenance, and operation of bridge.”
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "Construction, maintenance, and operation of bridge," it implies public participation in infrastructure projects. However, the text is purely a legislative amendment instruction (striking out section titles from a table of contents or analysis) and contains no substantive policy language, procedural requirements, or references to outside parties. It is a technical editing instruction, not a mandate for participation.

opus.w: This is a clerical amendment that strikes two section titles from the Canal Zone Code's table of contents. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The mention of a bridge is only a section heading being removed, not a federal decision that involves outsiders.

The only tempting reading is to treat the "Construction, maintenance, and operation of bridge" heading as a sign of some decision process. That fails because the heading is simply being deleted. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.

It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, or coordination with entities outside the federal government. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
